newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close higher after French rebound.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close higher after French rebound.

text.p: Italian shares closed mostly higher on Monday, with industrials at the head of the pack, after the post-election recovery in French markets spilled over into other continental centres.

The all-share Mibtel index finished 0.58 percent higher at 12,158 while the blue chip Mib30 ended 0.62 percent higher at 18,077. The strength of the dollar and of the lira against the mark also gave support to the market.
French shares defied widespread expectations of a massive selloff and recovered in the afternoon as investors were prepared to give the new socialist government the benefit of the doubt.
Brokers said that receding hopes of an early interest rate cut had not weighed heavily on the market although utilities, such as Edison had retreated.
Telecom stocks were also listless, also apparently reflecting interest rate disappointment, with Telecom Italia almost unchanged and Stet 0.32 percent lower at 8,522 lire.
Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said at the weekend that he would not hesitate to raise interest rates if inflation picked up.
Bellwether stocks Fiat and ENI also performed strongly, gaining 1.42 percent to 5,652 lire and 1.75 percent to 8,624 lire respectively.
